messages.author: 8498c5a7c566cf76
messages.subject: Large Bivariate Spatial Model
parts:
Dear List,

I would like to fit a bivariate spatial model to a large (55,000 records at 10,000 locations) data set. The key thing is that in addition to fitting separate scale parameters for each response variable, I need to be able to fit an additional scale parameter that controls the behaviour of the cross-covariance between the two responses as a function of distance.  Such a model is described in Section 2.2 of Gneiting et al's  "Matérn cross-covariance functions for multivariate random fields". I have yet to use INLA and I was wondering whether anybody could give me an indication whether such a model would be feasible before I set to learning how to use it?  

Thank you.

Jarrod

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Large Bivariate Spatial Model
parts:
Hi,

but please do not that a subset of such models ("coregionalization
models" I think is the common term) can be obtained as two linear
combinations of two (or more) independent SPDE models, and I believe
that can be achieved in INLA using the "copy" feature.

Finn

messages.author: bbb9357156c132fe
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Large Bivariate Spatial Model
parts:
It can estimate the cross-covariance. The general form is

y_1 ~ b_{11} f_1 + b_{12} f_2
y_2 ~ b_{21} f_1 + b_{22} f_2
where b_{21} = b_{12} is (related to) the cross covariance.

(here f_1 and f_2 are independent Gaussian random fields, possibly
with different parameters)

D

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Large Bivariate Spatial Model
parts:
Hi Daniel,

I need something of the form (e.g for the exponential covariance function):

COV(y_1,y_1) = c_{11}*exp(?d/a_{11})
COV(y_1,y_2) = c_{12}*exp(?d/a_{12})
COV(y_2,y_2) = c_{22}*exp(?d/a_{22})

where d is the distance between observations, and having a_12 as a
free parameter is the critical bit. If I understand your notation
correctly (and I may not have!) the regression of one spatial process
on the other is held constant so that COV(y_1,y_2)/COV(y_1,y_1)
remains the same for all d?

Cheers,

Jarrod
